 Order
Challenge is made in the present petition to the orders Annexures P-5 and P-6 dated 07.10.2016 and 25.04.2017 respectively.

2. By the order Annexure P-5, the Collector has rejected the application for making reference to the Court finding the application filed by the petitioner to be barred by time being filed beyond the limitation as provided in terms of Section 18(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
By the order Annexure P-2 review application for reviewing the said order has been rejected.

3. The brief facts as stated by learned counsel for the petitioner are that the land of the petitioner Krishna Kumar Namdeo vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194360978/
1 was subject to acquisition and award Annexure P-3 dated 07.02.2013 was passed.

sentences.text: Thereafter, the petitioner filed a writ petition before this Court on 04.01.2016, wherein it was prayed that the respondents be directed to refer the matter of proper assessment of compensation to the Court.
This petition was disposed of vide order dated 10.03.2016 and the petitioner was permitted to withdraw the petition with liberty to invoke the provisions of Section 18 of land Acquisition Act, 1984.
It is the case of the petitioner that when he approached the Collector, the Collector has rejected the application for referring the matter on the ground that the same is barred by limitation.
4. It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that once this Court had given liberty to approach the Collector under Section 18 of Act, 1894, the aspect of limitation got wiped off.

Learned counsel further submits that the application before the Collector for referring the matter duly contained pleadings that petitioner had submitted objections before the Land Acquisition Officer on 19.07.2013 and then again on 13.10.2014 and when no response was received, then he approached this Court.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further relies on judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Manharlal Shivlal Panchal and others vs. The Deputy Collector and Special Land Acquisition Officer and others 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1707.

sentences.text:
5. Per contra, it is contended by learned Panel Lawyer for the State that there is no provision for codonation of delay in availing remedy under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act and therefore, the authority has not committed any error in passing the orders Annexure P-5 and P-6.
6.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7. Section 18(2) of the Land Acquisition Act provides special limitation to make an application before the Collector for referring the dispute to the Court.
In case, the party was represented or present before the Collector, then the limitation is six weeks from the date of award.

In other cases,
it is within six weeks of receipt of notice from the Collector under Section 12(2) or within six months from the date of Collector's award whichever is early.
8. In the present case, the petitioner admittedly approached the Collector with request under Section 18 of the Act on 21.03.2016.

The copy of application filed before this Court as Annexure P-4-B has the date of presentation as 21.03.2016 on the front page, but the date at the bottom of application is typed as 21.03.2013, which is erroneous because the application itself contains events upto the year 2016.
9. The award was passed on 07.02.2013 and the petitioner approached to the Collector on 21.03.2016, i.e. after a period of three years and one month.
Even the writ petition before this Court was filed in January, 2016, which is after a period of two years and 10 months from the date of award.
Thus, the application before the Collector was clearly time barred and the petitioner even in approaching this Court in Writ Petition No.99/2016 was clearly raising a highly belated claim.
It is settled in law that the limitation as provided under Section 18(2) cannot be enlarged and the delay cannot be condoned.

The law on this point is well settled in Officer on Special Duty (Land Acquisition) vs. Shah Manilal Chandulal, (1996) 9 SCC 414, wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held as under:-

sentences.text: The right to make application in writing is provided under Section 18(1).
The proviso to sub-section (2) prescribes the limitation within which the said right would be exercised by the claimant or dissatisfied owner.

In Mohd. Hasnuddin v. State of Maharashtra [(1979) 2 SCC 572] , this Court was called upon to decide in a reference under Section 18 made by the Collector to the court beyond the period of limitation,
whether the court can go behind the reference and determine the compensation,
though the application for reference under Section 18 was barred by limitation?

entities.text: Mohd. Hasnuddin v. State of Maharashtra [(1979) 2 SCC 572]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court had held that the Collector is required under Section 18 to make a reference on the fulfilment of certain conditions, namely, (i) written application by interested person who has not accepted the award; (ii) nature of the objections taken for not accepting the award; and (iii) time within which the application shall be made.

In paragraph 22 after elaborating those conditions as conditions precedent to be fulfilled, it held that the power to make a reference under Section 18 is circumscribed by the conditions laid down therein and one such condition is a condition regarding limitation to be found in the proviso.
The Collector acts as a statutory authority.
If the application is not made within time, the Collector will not have the power to make reference.

In order to determine the limitation on his own power, the Collector will have to decide whether the application presented by the claimant is or is not within time and specify the conditions laid down under Section 18.

Even if the reference is wrongly made by the Collector, the court will have to determine the validity of the reference because the very jurisdiction of the court to hear a reference depends upon a proper reference being made under Section 18.
If the reference is not proper there is no jurisdiction in the court to hear the reference.

It was, therefore, held that it is the duty of the court to see that the statutory conditions laid down in Section 18 including the one relating to limitation, have been complied with and the application is not time-barred.
It is not debarred from satisfying itself that the reference which it is called upon to hear is a valid reference.
It has to proceed to determine compensation and if it is time-barred, it is not called upon to hear the same.
It is only a valid reference which gives jurisdiction to the court.
Therefore, the court has to ask itself the question whether it has jurisdiction to entertain the reference.
If the reference is beyond the prescribed period by the proviso to sub-section (2) of Section 18 of the Act and if it finds that it was not so made, the court would decline to answer the reference.
Accordingly, it was held that since the reference was made beyond the limitation, the court was justified in refusing to answer the reference.

9. It would thus be clear that one of the conditions precedent to make a valid reference to the court is that the application under Section 18(1) shall be in writing and made within six weeks from the date of the award when the applicant was present either in person or through counsel, at the time of making of the award by the Collector under clause (a) of proviso to sub-section (2).

The Collector, when he makes the reference, acts as a statutory authority.
10. In State of Punjab v. Satinder Bir Singh [(1995) 3 SCC 330] , a Bench of two Judges (to which one of us, K. Ramaswamy, J., was a member) was to consider Krishna Kumar Namdeo vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194360978/

sentences.text: whether the application for reference under Section 18 was barred by limitation and the direction issued by the court for making reference was valid in law.
The Collector made the award on 1-8-1970.
The notice under Section 12(2) was received by the respondent on 22-9-1970 and he received the compensation under protest on 29-9-1970.
The application for reference under Section 18 was made on 21-1-1971.
The Collector rejected the application as being barred by limitation.

The High Court in revision under Section 115, CPC, similar to Gujarat Amendment, allowed the revision holding that since the notice did not contain all the details of the award,
notice under Section 12(2) was not valid.
Therefore, there was no limitation.

This Court reversing the view had held in paragraph 7 that the form of notice was not material since the respondent appeared and received the notice on 22-9-1970 and received the compensation under protest on 29-9-1970.

The limitation began to run from the date of the receipt of the notice and by operation of clause (b) of the proviso to sub-section (2) of Section 18 since the application was not made within six weeks from the date of the receipt of the notice, the application was barred by limitation prescribed in Section 18(2).
It does not depend on the ministerial act of communication of notice in any particular form which the Act or rules have not prescribed.
The limitation began to operate from the moment the notice under Section 12(2) was received as is envisaged by Section 18(2).
Accordingly the order of the High Court was set aside.

18. Though hard it may be, in view of the specific limitation provided under proviso to Section 18(2) of the Act, we are of the considered view that sub-section (2) of Section 29 cannot be applied to the proviso to sub-section (2) of Section 18.
The Collector/LAO, therefore, is not a court when he acts as a statutory authority under Section 18(1).
Therefore, Section 5 of the Limitation Act cannot be applied for extension of the period of limitation prescribed under proviso to sub-section (2) of Section 18.
The High Court, therefore, was not right in its finding that the Collector is a court under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.

19. Accordingly, we hold that the applications are barred by limitation and the Collector has no power to extend time for making an application under Section 18(1)
for reference to the court."

10. Further in the case Mahadeo Bajirao Patil vs. State of Maharashtra, (2005) 7 SCC 440, it has been held as under:-
"14.

sentences.text: We are here not concerned with the correctness of the decision, but the fact remains that having considered the claim of the appellant for compensation, the Special Land Acquisition Officer rejected the claim.
This does amount to the making of an award, commonly described as "nil award".
If the appellant was aggrieved by such an award, it was open to him to seek reference under Section 18 of the Act which the appellant actually did.

We, therefore, cannot hold that no award as envisaged by Section 11 of the Act was declared on 29-8-1994, since the claim of the appellant was Krishna Kumar Namdeo vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194360978/
4 considered and was totally rejected.

sentences.text: There was, therefore, no question of giving any calculation of the manner in which the compensation was computed.

Since, the application under Section 18 was not filed within six weeks of the receipt of notice under Section 12(2) of the Act, the High Court did not commit any error in holding that the application was barred by limitation.

It was not disputed before us that the Land Acquisition Officer making a reference, or the Court considering a reference under Section 18 of the Act has no power of condonation of delay in making an application under the aforesaid section.

15. The next ground on which the High Court held the application to be barred by limitation is that in any event the appellant had knowledge of the award being made on 8-12- 1994, since he filed a copy of the award as annexure to the writ petition filed on 9-12-1994 and, therefore, should have filed the application under Section 18 of the Act within six weeks.

The submission urged on behalf of the appellant relying upon the decision of this Court in Raja Harish Chandra Raj Singh v. Dy. Land Acquisition Officer [(1962) 1 SCR 676 : AIR 1961 SC 1500] that in the instant case even if it is assumed that the appellant had knowledge of the award at least on 8-12-1994, he could make an application within six months from the date of such knowledge, would have deserved serious consideration, but for the finding recorded by us earlier that the appellant had notice under Section 12(2) of the Act and, therefore, t h e period of limitation for filing the application under Section 18 was six weeks from the date of receipt of the notice and not six months from the date of knowledge of the award.
1 1 .

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner has relied on the case of Manharlal Shivlal Panchal and others (supra).
In the aforesaid judgment, the fact was totally different.
In the said case, the land owner had challenged the acquisition proceedings as well as the award before the High Court and the matter reached upto the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
The SLP was dismissed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court on 11.04.2013 and thereafter, the reference proceedings were instituted.
12. Hon'ble the Supreme Court in Para 17 of the aforesaid judgment has held that it is settled in law that limitation for making reference under Section 18 of Act of 1894 cannot be extended.

However, it was held that since the acquisition proceedings were initially challenged and in terms of liberty given by the High Court, the land owners initiated reference proceedings within a period of six months from the date of dismissal of SLP.
On such facts, it was held that in fact, there is no delay in initiating the reference application.
13. The facts of this case are totally different.
The petitioner for the first time approached this Court by filing writ petition after a period of two years and ten months from the date of award.
There is no averment in the petition that the petitioner had no knowledge of the award.
The reference application (Annexure P-4-B) mentioned that the petitioner had for the first time contacted the Land Acquisition Officer on 19.07.2013.

Thus, it is clear that the petitioner had knowledge Krishna Kumar Namdeo vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194360978/
5 of award at least on 19.07.2013.
14.

entities.text: Krishna Kumar Namdeo vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 11 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner has also failed to bring any material on record to show that they had in fact submitted any application for referring the matter to the Court before Collector prior to approaching this Court, which remained undecided before the respondent authority.
It appears that the petitioner for the first time approached this Court in January, 2016 and withdrew their petition with liberty to approach the Collector.

15. Even the order passed in W.P. No.99/2016 does not enlarge the period of limitation, because this Court simply allowed withdrawal of Writ Petition with liberty to institute proceedings under Section 18 of the Act.

This Court did not enlarge the period of limitation and such enlargement of limitation cannot be deemed by necessary implication also because even the writ petition was filed after the limitation under Section 18 of Act of 1894 had expired long ago.
1 6 . Thus, the present case is squarely covered by the decisions of Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of Officer on Special Duty (Land Acquisition) (supra) and Mahadeo Bajirao Patil (supra).
The petition is devoid of merits and is dismissed.

However, it is observed that in terms of the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Bhagwan Das v. State of U.P., (2010) 3 SCC 545 , the petitioner would always be at the liberty to make an application under Section 28-A of the Act on the basis of an award of the Court in respect of other lands covered by the same acquisition notification, if there is an increase.

entities.text: Bhagwan Das v. State of U.P., (2010) 3 SCC 545
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 17. With the aforesaid observations, the petition is dismissed.
